dedupe_keys.name: epa all hazards waste management planning tool

description: The All-Hazards Waste Management Planning Tool is an interactive web application from the US Environmental Protection Agency that guides communities through writing a pre-incident plan for managing the materials and waste from natural and human-made disasters. It is aimed at emergency managers and planners in states, local governments, tribes and territories and at large facilities such as airports and stadiums. The tool walks users through each planning step, from estimating waste types and quantities and choosing staging sites to arranging contracts, and prepares them to put the plan into action after an incident; it links to guidance, example state and local debris plans, training and safety resources. It covers the United States and all hazards. The tool is free to use online and has a user's guide from April 2025 and a recorded webinar. Content is a US government work; the page stresses that the tool is not a regulation and creates no legal requirements. Caveats: it produces planning documents, not quantitative model outputs, and planners must still check federal, state and local rules. Simulation uses: a structured source of plan assumptions, such as staging sites and contracted capacity, for disaster debris and waste logistics models. Related records: the EPA Disaster Debris Recovery Tool (data-epa-disaster-debris-recovery-tool) locates facilities, and the EPA All Hazards Waste Logistics Tool (model-epa-all-hazards-waste-logistics-tool) estimates transport cost and time.
